clue.text: Mineral brought down, said Pole

indicators.note: said tells us the word for brought down is to be heard rather than spelt as usual

parts.note: a tree brought down has been felled
a spar is a pole, as on a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: A rock seemingly lowered while someone from Poland speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' acts on FELLED only, giving FELD; 'Pole' is a length of wood, not a person from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is a common rock-forming mineral group found in granite.

clue.text: An old letter from Goethe

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the German poet's name

explanation.surface: A historic piece of correspondence penned by the German writer Goethe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is an Old English and Icelandic character for the th sound, now obsolete in English.

clue.text: Snack one's left to boil over

indicators.note: left here means left out, so the words one's are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to do one's nut is British slang for to lose one's temper, to boil over with rage

explanation.surface: A snack someone has forgotten on the stove, allowed to bubble over.
explanation.walkthrough: DO ONE'S NUT, British slang for flying into a rage, loses ONE'S, as 'one's left' instructs, leaving DO NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A donut, the American spelling of doughnut, is a sweet fried snack.

clue.text: Racing driver considered to have gone flat out

parts.note: Alain Prost is a French Formula One world champion
rated means considered or judged

explanation.surface: A racing driver reckoned to have driven at full throttle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' suggests top speed, but here it means lying stretched on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrated means laid face down and stretched out, so lying full length on the ground.

clue.text: Announce as unsuitable function of playground

parts.note: rec is British short for recreation ground, a public playing field
a function is a use or purpose

explanation.surface: Declaring a playground's role inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: To recuse is to declare a judge or juror disqualified from a case, for example through a conflict of interest.

clue.text: Delegate's record in service

indicators.note: in puts the word for a record inside the word for service

parts.note: duty is service owed, as in military duty
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An envoy's track record in public service.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is someone appointed to act on another's behalf, as a delegate does.

clue.text: Died on boat? That's not fair

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogy
the ark was Noah's boat

explanation.surface: Someone protests that dying aboard a ship is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' means light-coloured, as in hair or complexion, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark hair or skin is the opposite of fair, which means pale or blond.

clue.text: Ladies: what one does there, having first taken off clothes

parts.note: in the Ladies, the toilet, one goes to pee

indicators.note: having first taken off means the opening letter of the word for clothes is removed

parts.note: dresses are clothes

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction about using the women's toilet after undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' points to a toilet in the wordplay but defines noblewomen.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeresses are women holding a peerage or married to peers, addressed as Lady.

clue.text: Bad steer, to incite one who may go out on a limb

definitions.text: one who may go out on a limb

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of steer are spoilt and put in a new order

parts.note: to urge on is to incite or spur

explanation.surface: Steering badly might provoke someone into taking a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out on a limb' sounds like risk-taking; here it is literal, climbing out along a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist climbing to prune trees must literally edge out along branches.

clue.text: Faith very receptive to suggestion

indicators.note: receptive to means the word for very takes in the word for suggestion

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
a hint is a suggestion

explanation.surface: Belief that is highly open to persuasion, like a hypnotic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on worship of kami spirits.

clue.text: Selector's remarkable piece of armoury

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable: the letters are marked out afresh in another order

parts.note: the word selector supplies the letters; the 's is short for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A team selector's notable item from a weapons collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A corselet is a piece of body armour covering the torso.

clue.text: In the last month in college, apply to do lots together

indicators.note: in places the word for last month within the college's initials

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
ult, short for ultimo, means of the last month in old commercial letters
to apply to someone is to ask them

explanation.surface: Last month at college, applying to do several things at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To multitask is to handle several jobs at the same time.

clue.text: Second-hand story of papal toe?

parts.note: Urban is a name taken by several popes
the toe is at the leg end, the end of the leg

explanation.surface: A rumour about the pope's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically the phrase is Urban's leg end, Pope Urban's toe.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban legend is an apocryphal tale passed on as true, heard from a friend of a friend.

clue.text: Religious celebration fixed around 2nd February

indicators.note: around has the word for fixed surround the chosen letter

parts.note: fast means fixed firmly, as in stuck fast

indicators.note: 2nd picks the second letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A church holiday set near the start of February, like Candlemas.
explanation.walkthrough: '2nd February' looks like a date, but means the second letter of February.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a religious festival, such as a saint's day in the church calendar.

clue.text: Fiery spirit of monk bringing round power tool

indicators.note: bringing round has the tool's name placed around the monk

parts.note: a sander is an electric tool for smoothing wood
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A spirited monk wielding an electric tool.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore the salamander is an elemental spirit believed to live in fire.

clue.text: Put up with a lecturer from the north

parts.note: to have borne something is to have put up with it; bore is its past tense

explanation.surface: Tolerating a teacher from northern parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreal means northern, from Boreas, the Greek north wind.

clue.text: After-dinner speaker perhaps disturbs our trance

indicators.note: disturbs suggests the letters of our trance are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A long-winded speaker after a meal breaks our drowsy daze.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, the sort hired to speak after a banquet.

clue.text: Some may say sex worker has a stout rope

indicators.note: some may say signals a sound-alike, true only in accents that drop the final r

parts.note: a whore is a sex worker, and whore's a is whore has a run together

explanation.surface: A prostitute owns a thick rope, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'whore's a' and HAWSER are said alike, hence the hedge 'Some may say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: What one may hear from horse thief

definitions.text: What one may hear from horse
definitions.meaning: the soft whinny of a horse
one who nicks, British slang for steals

explanation.surface: A noise from a horse, or from a horse thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for steal, so a nicker is a thief; the noun also names a horse's low neigh.

clue.text: Owns toboggan, endless bother

parts.note: has means owns

indicators.note: endless means the word for toboggan loses its final letter

parts.note: a sled is a toboggan

explanation.surface: Having a sledge that never stops is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is trouble or annoyance, a near synonym of bother.

clue.text: Become endlessly stupid, and like horror stories

parts.note: go can mean become, as in go mad

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for stupid loses its last letter

parts.note: thick is British slang for stupid

explanation.surface: Turning ever more foolish, as in a horror tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction is the genre of eerie, macabre tales such as Dracula and Frankenstein.

clue.text: Refuse to vote for 13

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to cast a no vote, so refuse to back something
the answer to 13, a feast; British slang for a party or celebration

explanation.definitionFit: A beano is an informal British word for a lively party or blowout meal, a feast.

clue.text: Pastry not very short, value doubtful

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the letters are in an uncertain, jumbled order
short says the word very is cut down to its first letter, its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Pastry not very skimpy, of questionable worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a pastry description; it shortens 'very' to V.
explanation.definitionFit: A vol-au-vent is a small, light puff pastry case with a savoury filling.

clue.text: There you are in France, picking up one instrument

indicators.note: picking up shifts the letter for one earlier in the French phrase

parts.note: voila is French for there you are
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French shop assistant handing over a single instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a stringed instrument of the violin family, slightly larger than the violin.

clue.text: Member with independent opinion

parts.note: M stands for member, as in MP, member of parliament
Ind is the abbreviation for independent, as in election results

explanation.surface: An MP of independent views.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind means opinion, as in to speak one's mind or change one's mind.

clue.text: In search for compliments maybe, always a bit frenzied

indicators.note: in puts the word for always inside the word for searching

parts.note: to fish is to search for something, as in fishing for compliments
ever means always

explanation.surface: Constantly angling for praise makes one somewhat frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means in a state of agitated excitement, slightly frantic.

clue.text: A little fluid, say, not a condition full of it

parts.note: a drop is a little fluid

indicators.note: not tells us the word a is taken out of the word for say

explanation.surface: A little fluid, so to speak, is no illness brimming with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to the fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for oedema, the swelling caused by excess fluid in body tissue.

clue.text: Star students on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A star pupil climbing the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

clue.text: Really enjoyed a party, looking flushed

parts.note: a do is a party
red means flushed in the face

explanation.surface: Someone loved a party and came away pink-cheeked.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored is used loosely for liked very much, as in I adored that film.

clue.text: Death — by hanging?

definitions.meaning: ... is slang for death or the end, as in it's ... for him
things hung at a window, so they come by hanging

explanation.definitionFit: Curtains is slang for the end or death, and literally means drapes that hang at windows.
